instruction: Use Abaqus to perform a torsion analysis of a circular shaft (Variant B). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Revolution. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (6, 72) in the X-Y plane, using the left vertical edge at X = 0 as the revolution axis (global Y-axis). Revolve 360 deg to generate a solid cylinder with diameter 12 mm and length 72 mm, aligned with the global Y-axis. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Steel and assign it to the entire shaft. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the shaft. Analysis Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Torque-B. Constraints and Boundary Conditions: Create a reference point RP-1 at the center of the free end face (Y = 72 mm, X = 0, Z = 0). Apply a kinematic coupling constraint between the free end face and RP-1, coupling all 6 degrees of freedom. Apply an Encastre boundary condition to the fixed end face at Y = 0. Loading: Apply a torque (Moment) of 920 N*mm at RP-1 about the shaft axis (global Y-axis, component MY). Discretization: Mesh the shaft with a global seed size of 4 mm. Assign the element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-Torsion-B, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Post-Processing: Open the output database. Review the Mises stress contour. Query the RP-1 rotation magnitude (UR). Query the shear stress components at any node located on the shaft outer surface (radius approximately 6 mm). Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Torsion-B.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Torsion-B.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
